summary: On-demand activity replay with per-event checksum, redact-explain artifacts, and signed manifest for SAR evidence
description:
Issue summary:
IvyBank requests a reproducible playback bundle for a 2-hour production window (2026-03-08 09:00:00 to 11:00:00 UTC) for Subject Access Request (SAR) evidence. The bundle must include: (1) per-event checksums (SHA256) validated against our export, (2) reversible/redaction rationale metadata for any PII-suppressed fields, (3) a signed manifest (ed25519) produced by Redwood using their provided public key, and (4) a resume/nonce token so the customer can verify continuity when ingesting into their forensics system.

Impact:
Customer needs this bundle to satisfy a regulatory SAR deadline and to provide an auditable chain of custody to their internal compliance team. Delay > 48 hours is impacting legal review calendar.

Environment:
Production, eu-west region. Customer uses a dedicated account with enterprise tier entitlements and BYOK for manifest verification (they supplied an ed25519 public key).

Requested deliverables (customer-specified):
- Compact ndjson replay of the 2-hour activity window, ordered by event_time, gzip-compressed.
- Per-event SHA256 checksum field named "event_checksum" in the record envelope.
- Redaction rationale metadata attached per record (field: "redaction_rationale") explaining why a field was masked (algorithmic, policy-id, operator-id).
- A signed manifest (manifest.json.sig) covering the bundle, anchor hash, and resume token; signature algorithm ed25519.
- Resume token/nonce for the bundle start and end (for resumable ingest).
- A short Q&A explaining how reversible pseudonymization was applied and how keys are rotated.

Steps to reproduce / notes for Support engineers:
1) Validate the exact tenant_id and time window with customer (customer-provided event sample attached in comment).
2) Run ordered export job with per-event checksum generation using export tool v2.3.
3) Apply reversible pseudonymization audit trail to records where PII suppressed; include redaction rationale.
4) Produce manifest with anchor hash (SHA256 over compressed payload) and sign with Redwood artifact signing key; include customer's supplied ed25519 pubkey for verifiable signature example.
5) Upload bundle to the customer's secure S3 presigned location and provide delivery receipt.

Logs / attachments referenced:
- Console export job: https://redwood.console/exports/exp-68812
- Customer sample events (provided in initial ticket comment).

Notes: This is not a full forensic replay toolchain request; customer only asked for an evidence bundle and explanatory notes to hand to their legal team.

investigation_notes: Confirmed tenant: ivy-prod-42 via account mapping in org-service (org-9876).
Export job exp-68812 ran on prod eu-west nodes (srv-gpu-14, srv-gpu-17). Observed IO wait spikes at t=+45m due to shard rebalancer; mitigated by throttling rebalances during export window.
Checksum generation performed with export-tool v2.3 --sha256 option. Verified sample checksums locally against original events and match sample provided by customer.
Redaction rationale attached using schema v1.1 (fields: policy_id, masking_algorithm, operator_id, timestamp). Security performed schema review, minor tweak to include rotation_id field for clarity.

Manifest produced: manifest.json includes: bundle_id, tenant_id, window_start, window_end, compressed_size_bytes, anchor_sha256, resume_token_start, resume_token_end. Signed with redwood-ops-ed25519 key (sig file manifest.json.sig).
No reversible pseudonymization keys shared with customer; provided documentation describing transformation and key rotation cadence (KMS rotation every 90 days, key identifiers included in runbook).
Prepared small runbook with command-line verification steps: compute SHA256 on downloaded file, verify manifest anchor, verify ed25519 signature using customer's pubkey and example code snippet.
Linked internal PR for export-tool minor change: github.com/redwood-inference/exports/commit/ab3f9d2 (adds rotation_id to redaction rationale).

Security attestation from Omar Khan included with bundle saying redaction rationale schema and reversible mapping documentation meet customer's requested evidence standard. No key material was shared; only algorithm and rotation metadata provided.
